extracted.subtask_short: news reporting on corporate safety settlement
extracted.subtask_description: A mainstream news article reporting on a corporate deferred prosecution agreement and settlement relating to vehicle safety defects and alleged concealment. Focuses on investigative findings, official statements, and the timeline of reporting and recalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misleading consumers by concealing safety issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Toyota 'misled U.S. consumers by concealing and making deceptive statements about two safety related issues affecting its vehicles, each of which caused a type of unintended acceleration.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the deferred prosecution agreement language quoted in the article; frames concealment and deceptive public statements as the central legal allegation leading to the agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to recall cars with known problem parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Not only did Toyota fail to recall cars with problem parts, they continued to manufacture new cars with the same parts they already knew were deadly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FBI Assistant Director George Venizelos' statement characterizes failure to recall as a key wrongdoing; the article cites examples (floor mats, sticky pedals) and alleges recalls were insufficient in scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing manufacture/use of known-dangerous parts
rubrics_metrics.description: The company 'continued to manufacture new cars with the same parts they already knew were deadly.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as aggravating conduct in the DOJ/FBI account — manufacturing vehicles with parts known to cause fatalities intensifies the alleged misconduct beyond mere omission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recalls must comprehensively address known dangers (recall scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: ABC News reports that announced recalls 'did not cover all the cars they knew were in danger' and earlier recalls addressing floor-mat-related issues missed other causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article contrasts announced recalls (e.g., floor mats) with later revelations that recalls failed to cover all affected vehicles and did not address 'sticky' pedals initially; implies expectation of comprehensive recall responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about all discovered defect causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Toyota concealed another cause of sudden acceleration they had found during investigations — 'sticky' pedals — and announced it only minutes before an ABC News report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The timing (announcement minutes before an ABC report) and the phrase 'concealed another cause' are used to underline lack of transparency; guidance implies companies should disclose all known defect causes promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate responsibility: prioritize safety over sales/profit
rubrics_metrics.description: The FBI statement: 'Toyota put sales over safety and profit over principle.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an ethical standard in the article; frames corporate decisions that place sales/profit ahead of consumer safety as unacceptable and central to the criticism and legal consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative journalism practices (expose, follow-up, build public record)
rubrics_metrics.description: ABC News 'first reported the potential dangers of unintended acceleration' in November 2009 and 'published dozens of reports' in following months, including exclusive investigations ('Runaway Toyotas').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article presents sustained, exclusive reporting and follow-up coverage as the mechanism that revealed additional issues and pressured disclosure; implies good investigative reporting involves initial exposure, ongoing follow-up, and building a documented record.
